linkedin:
Remote hiring managers read applications on a screen, between meetings, often in a second language. The applications that get a reply are easy to scan and clearly written for this role.

From the guide on writing a remote job application that gets read:

Lead with the role, not your life story. Open with the exact job title and where you saw it, then one sentence on why your recent work fits the team. Save the background for later.

Show proof of async work. Mention a project you ran with written updates, a shared document you owned, or a time zone gap you handled well.

Match their words. Read the job post twice. If they say “customer support”, do not write “client care”. Hiring software and tired humans look for the same words they wrote.

Keep the CV short and current. One clean page beats a long history. Lead with your most recent remote or freelance work, with what you shipped, not just what you were responsible for.

Follow up once, politely. If you hear nothing after a week, send one short note restating your fit. One clear follow-up reads as professional; more reads as pressure.

Save this for your next application.
